# HW 3 Plotting a Tennis Player's Career from Tennis Abstract

<!-- #region -->
## Purpose

The purpose of this assignment was to develop a package that could extract a professional tennis player's career from [Tennis Abstract](https://www.tennisabstract.com/), a website that records the match statistics of professional tennis players' matches throughout their career. 

### Package Contents
This package contains two main functions: `getcareertable()` and `getcareerplot()`


`
getcareertable(name)
`

- Argument `name` is the tennis player's name in the format FirstLast in quotation marks.

- A data frame containing five columns:
    - "Date"
    - "Player_Age"
    - "Opponent_Age"
    - "Age_Difference"
    - "Player_Outcome"

*for more information, see `getcareertable_DICTIONARY.txt` in /R/ folder*


`
getcareerplot(table, name = "PlayerName")
`

- Argument `name` is optional and is the tennis player's name in the format FirstLast in quotation marks. By default, it will show use "PlayerName" to display on the plot

- Argument `table` is the table from getcareertable()

- A scatter plot of all matches a professional tennis player has won or lost in their career, and their age relative to their opponents each match. The layout of the plot is directly influenced by the one created for Serena Williams in the New York Times article ["Serena Williams Dominated Her Generation, Then the Next One, Too."](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2022/08/28/sports/tennis/serena-age-opponents.html) by Leo Dominguez and Sara Ziegler.

``` r
williams_tbl
williams_plt = getcareerplot(williams_tbl)
```

``` r
#testing with a male tennis player
``` 

## Special Considerations

### Omitted Data
- When extracting the data from Tennis Abstract in the form of .js (Javascript) files, there were lines that were missing either an tennis player's opponent's birthday or age, for female and male players respectively. I tracked these using the `unincluded_indices` variable in the auxiliary functions `getwomensoppsbdays()` and `getmensoppsages()`. I then used `unincluded_indices` to omit those lines from all future calculations.

### Inaccessible Data
- Some player's data could not be extracted because the URLs for the .js files did not exist. An example was for the player Ben Shelton. Try `https://www.tennisabstract.com/jsmatches/BenShelton.js` in your browser (I used Google Chrome). This is not the case for Serena Williams, and this url `https://www.tennisabstract.com/jsmatches/SerenaWilliams.js` will open. This package is, therefore, not suited for every player on Tennis Abstract. For future directions, I might explore extracting data in different ways. 


## Reflection

### Translation 
- The hardest part of this project had been translating the code I had created to replicate the New York Times plot of Serena Williams's career for this project. That code is under the repository `UCB-stat159-f26/hw02-chloeomeanylucas` on GitHub. When I cleaned the data, I tailored all steps directly to the composition of the data. For example, when I wanted to remove an empty row, I used a negative index. For this project, I instead used `[!is.na()]` which is much more widely applicable to any length of data. It made me question whether I had been too narrow with my pipeline for plotting Williams' career, and how I might improve this in future projects. 

### Missing Data
- I realized halfway through creating my functions that there was missing data, for both male and female player's datasets from Tennis Abstract. I then had to check what had changed along my entire pipeline, omit the appropriate lines of data, and then try to see if it worked with different players. It was a tedious process, and it added more and more lines to my code. It is important, however, because I don't think the calculations could handle empty strings or NA values.
